work.text: It was created from 1312 to 1315 and is considered one of the artist's masterpieces and one of the most important examples of 14th-century Italian art.

In the Council Hall of Siena we see him in all his splendour. On one side, radiant in beauty, the Queen of Heaven sits in the midst of the noblest of the Saints, the loveliest of the Virgins, and the sweetest of the Angels.

source.author: Bernard Berenson
source.title: The Central Italian Painters of the Renaissance

moment.text: As in Duccio's Majestas at Siena, the four saintly protectors of the city are represented kneeling in the foreground.

The composition, too, has the defects of Duccio and is distributed without the perfect balance of the Florentines. It betrays the necessity under which the artist laboured, of preserving old forms of arrangement dictated by custom.

source.author: J. A. Crowe and G. B. Cavalcaselle
source.title: A History of Painting in Italy, vol. 3: The Sienese School of the Fourteenth Century (ed. Langton Douglas)
